question: An otherwise healthy 56-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-year history of intermittent upper abdominal pain. She has had no nausea, vomiting, or change in weight. Physical examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies are within normal limits. Abdominal ultrasonography shows a hyperechogenic rim-like calcification of the gallbladder wall. The finding in this patient's ultrasonography increases the risk of which of the following conditions?
analysis: The hyperechogenic rim-like calcification of the gallbladder wall seen on ultrasonography is highly suggestive of gallstones (cholelithiasis). This finding increases the risk of gallbladder carcinoma, particularly in patients with long-standing gallstones.
